head.meta_description: Catering menus in Dubai with published prices: packages from AED 1,200 to AED 5,500, per-person formats from AED 90, private chef from AED 700, and 11 dietary options.
head.h1: Catering Menus Dubai — Packages and Per-Person Prices

opening_paragraph: Catering menus in Dubai from myCHEF are priced two ways: as a package for a set group size, or per person by service format. Packages run from AED 1,200 for a date night to AED 5,500 for the full experience. Per-person formats start at AED 90 for a working lunch and AED 120 for an event buffet, with a plated private chef at AED 700 to AED 950 per head.

new_paragraphs: Date Night , 2 guests, from AED 1,200 — a bespoke three-course menu for two with a private chef, table service and full cleanup. Family Feast , 6 to 8 guests, from AED 2,400 — premium ingredients with chef and service support for a relaxed family dinner. Birthday Celebration , 8 to 12 guests, from AED 3,600 — canapes or a starter, main course, dessert and service staff.

Corporate Dinner , 10 to 15 guests, from AED 4,500 — a multi-course or buffet menu with service staff and formal presentation. The Full Experience , 6 to 10 guests, from AED 5,500 — a multi-course tasting menu, pairing consultation, a full service team and premium plating. Weekly Prep runs from AED 1,900 per week for 2 to 3 recurring meals, or AED 2,700 for larger households at 4 to 6.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What a sample evening looks like
new_paragraphs: A full tasting progression runs from an amuse-bouche through to dessert — scallops, sea bass, short rib, an artisan cheese course, and a Valrhona chocolate sphere with salted caramel and gold leaf to close. That is the top of the range instead of the default, and it is what the full experience package is built around.

Most evenings are simpler than that and better for it. Three or four courses executed properly beat seven stretched thin, and a shorter menu concentrates the kitchen's attention where it shows. If you are choosing between more courses and better ingredients, choose the ingredients.

add_block.new_heading: What it will cost to feed 40 guests
new_paragraphs: Multiply the per-head tier by your headcount and add 5% VAT — that is the whole calculation, and it is why the tiers are published. To feed 40 guests from a standard event buffet, work from AED 120 per person. The same 40 people at a working lunch start from AED 90 each; a premium buffet with live stations or a canape reception starts from AED 150. A plated private-chef dinner is a different product at AED 700 to AED 950 a head, and at 40 covers it needs a brigade instead of one chef, so most 40-guest events land in the buffet band.

Two things move the figure after that, and both are quoted as their own lines instead of being buried in the per-head number. Staffing is the first: drop-off trays need nobody on site, a buffet needs someone maintaining it for the length of service, and live stations need a chef standing at each one. Rentals are the second — furniture, linen, crockery and glassware for 40 rarely already exist in a villa, and hiring them is a real cost that some quotes hide. At 40 guests you are well clear of every minimum, so the only question left is which format you want.

add_block.new_heading: What makes a good catering menu
new_paragraphs: A good catering menu is short, seasonal and built around what a kitchen can genuinely hold at temperature for the length of your event. Ideas are never the shortage in menu planning; the discipline is cutting. Four dishes cooked properly beat nine that arrive lukewarm, and every extra item takes attention away from the ones your guests will remember.

The best catering menus in Dubai also do three unglamorous things well. They give every dish a one-line description that says what is in it, so a guest with a dietary requirement can self-select without having to ask anyone. They balance the room — something substantial, something light, and at least one vegetarian dish nobody has to apologise for. And they respect the weather: an outdoor menu in July is built from dishes that survive the heat, which is not the same menu you would serve at the same villa in January.

new_paragraphs: Eleven diets are handled as standard: vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, halal, kosher, dairy-free, nut-free, keto, pescatarian, low-sodium and diabetic-friendly. Halal is the default across our menus instead of a request you have to make.

Flag requirements at enquiry with the guest count instead of in the final 48 hours, and say how severe they are — a preference and an allergy need different plans. Food-safety training sits behind it: ICCA Dubai sets out that every handler, supervisor and Person in Charge under Dubai Municipality must hold approved training, with a certified Person in Charge carrying legal responsibility.

new_paragraphs: How much do catering menus cost in Dubai?

Packages run from AED 1,200 for a date night to AED 5,500 for the full experience. Per-person formats start at AED 90 for a working lunch, AED 120 for an event buffet and AED 150 for BBQ, live stations or canapes, with a plated private chef at AED 700 to AED 950.
Which format is the most economical?

A working or office lunch at AED 90 per person is the lowest per-head tier, and a standard event buffet at AED 120 is the usual choice for a party. What you pay above that is labour, not food quality.
How much will it cost to feed 40 guests?

Take the per-head tier and multiply by 40, then add 5% VAT. A standard event buffet works from AED 120 per person, a working lunch from AED 90, and a premium buffet or canape reception from AED 150. Staffing and rentals are quoted separately.
Do you have menus for a small party?

Yes. The Date Night package covers two guests and the Family Feast six to eight, so a small party is a normal booking. For a standing reception, canapes and other finger food suit a small group better than a seated menu. Volume formats start at 10 guests, or 20 for a buffet.
What is the leading catering company in Dubai?

No independent ranking of Dubai catering companies exists, so treat any top 10 list as advertising unless it publishes its method. Judge on what you can check yourself: published prices, a stated minimum, who holds the food licence, and whether the quote is itemised.
Can I download the menus as a PDF?
There is no PDF to request. Every format, package and price is on this page instead of behind a download form, and the menu written for your event arrives as an itemised proposal.
What does the private chef experience include?
A chef cooking and plating each course for your table, from AED 950 per person. Packages bundle it with service, equipment and cleanup for set group sizes.
Do you offer weekly meal prep?
Yes. From AED 1,900 per week for 2 to 3 recurring sessions, or AED 2,700 for larger households at 4 to 6, with rotating menus, portioning, labelling and cleanup.
Which dietary requirements do you cover?
Eleven as standard: vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, halal, kosher, dairy-free, nut-free, keto, pescatarian, low-sodium and diabetic-friendly. Halal is the default.
Is VAT included in the published prices?
Add 5%. UAE catering carries 5% VAT, introduced on 1 January 2018, and a clear proposal shows it as its own line.
Can you serve alcohol?
Alcohol service is controlled by venue licensing instead of by the caterer. We design the non-alcoholic programme and coordinate with your venue's licensed provider.

new_paragraphs: Where a package does not fit the shape of your event, the same food is priced per head by format. A working or office lunch starts at AED 90 per person. A standard event buffet starts at AED 120 . Premium buffet, BBQ, live stations and canapes start at AED 150 . The private chef experience , plated course by course at your table, runs AED 700 to AED 950 .

The gap between AED 150 and AED 700 is not a food-quality difference; it is a labour difference. A buffet is set out once and maintained. A private chef cooks and plates every course for every guest, which is a different job and a different number of hours. Between those two sit the station formats, where a chef cooks in front of guests but serves many of them at a time. Decide the format first and the per-head figure follows from it.

Volume formats carry a minimum of 10 guests , or 20 for a buffet, and a minimum order of AED 900 . A plated private-chef dinner has no minimum headcount, which is why a table of two is a normal booking instead of an exception.
